Appearance:
 Shri Sohit Mishra Ga for the respondent/State.
 Order

This writ petition has been registered on the basis of the letter No.297, dated 26.6.2025 received from Special Judge, POCSO Act, District Datia and on account of directions issued vide order dated 20.2.2025 passed in W.P.No.5184/2025 (In Reference (Suo Motu) Versus The State of Madhya Pradesh and others) in which certain guidelines have been carved out in order to expedite the cases relating to termination of pregnancy under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (for short "the MTP Act").
2.

entities.text: Special Judge, POCSO Act, District Datia
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On the report of the victim's father the Police Station Dursada registered a crime under section 64 (2), 65 (1) BNS and 5L/6 POCSO Act under Crime No.50/2025 against the accused Neeraj Ahirwar son Parshuram Ahirwar, R/o Village Bhadevra, Police Station Unao District Datia MP, and during investigation, on the basis of the letter written by the Child Welfare Committee District Datia, Police station Dursada recovered the victim from Shakti Sadan Gwalior on 22.06.2025 and got her medical examination done
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13433 2 WP-25486-2025 at Civil Hospital, Morar, District Gwalior and ultrasound was done at JAH Gwalior.
The report of which was presented before the Special Judge and on 23.06.2025.

From the observation of the medical report,
it is evident that the pregnancy period of the victim is around 26 weeks.

Under the instructions of SOP dated 24.02.2025, the Chief Medical and Health Officer was directed to get the victim examined by the Medical Board at the District Hospital Datia and send a report to the Special Judge,

sentences.text: After examining the health condition of the victim on 25.06.2025, the Medical Board of District Hospital Datia has submitted a report that she has anemia and low platelets and the fetus weighs about one kg.

entities.text: Medical Board of District Hospital Datia
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According to the opinion given by the Medical Board, the life of the victim is in danger if her pregnancy is terminated.
The report dated 25.6.2025 given by the Medical Board is reproduced as under:

BP 110/66 mm/hg, pulse 72 b/m

Thus, this Court while passing the order has to keep in mind the report of Medical Board dated 25.6.2025, the future of a minor girl aged 13 years 10 months, who is carrying a foetus of a rapist, the trauma she will have to face throughout her life while raising such child and not only this the child will also have to live his/her entire life with such social stigma.
4. Section 3(1), 3 (2) (b) (i) and Section 5(1) of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 which reads as under :-
"3. When pregnancies may be terminated by registered medical practitioners.-(1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in the Indian Penal Code(45 of 1860), a registered medical practitioner shall not be guilty of any offence under that Code or under any other law for the time being in force, if any pregnancy is terminated by him in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

(2) Subject to the provisions of sub-section (4), a pregnancy may be terminated by a registered medical practitioner,-
Minor Prosecutrix X Through Father Shri ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122244283/
2 (a)...
(b) where the length of the pregnancy exceeds twelve weeks but does not exceed twenty weeks, if not less than two registered medical practitioners are, of opinion,
formed in good faith, that- (i) the continuance of the pregnancy would involve a risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to her physical or mental health.
5. Sections 3 and 4 when not to apply.-(1)

The provisions of section 4, and so much of the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 3 as relate to the length of the pregnancy and the opinion of not less than two registered medical practitioners, shall not apply to the termination of a pregnancy by a registered medical practitioner in a case where he is of opinion, formed in good faith, that the termination of such pregnancy is immediately necessary to save the life of the pregnant woman."
5. Nothing of the sort as provided in the aforesaid section exists in the present matter.

The Medical Board on the other hand had advised that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13433 4 WP-25486-2025 looking to the health status of the victim, abortion at this stage would be dangerous to her life.
6. Under these circumstances, no direction can be issued for medical termination of the pregnancy of the victim and therefore, the present petition is disposed of with the following directions:

( i) The District Hospital Datia shall bear all the expenses in regard to the hospitalization of the minor over the past week and in respect of her re- admission to the hospital for delivery as and when she is required to do so; and (ii) In the event that the minor and her parents desire to give the child in adoption after the delivery,
the State Government shall take all necessary steps in accordance with the applicable provisions of law to facilitate this exercise.
This shall not be construed as a direction of this Court binding either the parents or the minor and the State shall abide by the wishes as expressed at the appropriate stage.
( iii )
The State will provide all available medical facilities through specialist team of doctors to permit the victim to give birth to the child.
(iv) All the expenses shall be born by the State in connection with the procedure of giving birth to the child.
(v) All necessary care and cautions shall be taken by the doctors during the period of pregnancy and at the time of delivery of a child and thereafter as and when required.

sentences.text: 3 (vi) Post delivery care will be extended to the victim and it will be duty of the State Government to take care of the child as per the settled norms.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13433 5 WP-25486-2025 (vii)

In case the child is given in adoption, till it is adopted all medical facilities will be made available to the child by the State Government and if it is not adopted the said facility shall be given till the child attains majority.

(viii) The State Government shall consider to form a policy to provide the facilities for food, shelter,
education safety of the children given birth by the survivors of sexual assault, or rape or incest.
(ix) The identity of the girl and if she gives birth to a live child, then parentage of the child, shall be kept a secret and shall not be revealed to anybody.
This is being done looking to the future of the girl (prosecutrix).

(x) It is also directed that no legal claim can be put forth on the team of the doctors by the girl or her parents as they have understood the possible complications and the team of doctors will not be liable to any legal complications arising out of such procedure.
(xi) The District Hospital Datia may carry out DNA sampling of the baby and preserve report of such DNA sampling to be produced before the competent Court where criminal case is pending.

(xii) In addition, as an immediate respite, the State Government is directed to make payment of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh) as compensation, the State Government shall make a fixed deposit of a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs) in favour of the minor girl in any nationalized bank which will be given to her only when she reaches the age of 18 years.

The District Magistrate of the District where the family of girl chooses to live henceforth will ensure that bank account is opened in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13433 6 WP-25486-2025 name of the minor girl in any nationalized bank, chosen by her father.
It is made clear that at the maturity of the aforesaid fixed deposit, only she will be entitled to get the money.
7. With the aforesaid direction, this writ petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.

8. Let a copy of the order be provided to learned Govt. Advocate free of cost in a sealed cover for immediate transmission to the Civil Surgeon, District Hospital Datia and also to the concerned Court.
